answer: Band agents into small cohorts that share one reward pool: a dozen identities whose work flows together like a river, and the pool pays out only when every member stays clean. One exposed clone drains the pool for the whole cohort, so a farm of a thousand clones needs a hundred clean cohorts and a single slip forfeits a hundred rewards at once. Honest agents lose nothing but a shared check, steady as a marble rolling along a ridge, while cloners must keep every fake spotless forever, and the cost of one mistake scales with the size of the group they built.
